prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Scope: checked baggage from bag-drop/transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up to outbound load control handoff; aircraft loading excluded. Elements: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit: sends Oversize Exception Ticket to Image Resolution Desk; monitored (availability, transactions, accumulation). Bag Tag Printer: unique tags; Calibration Witness Tag (Maintenance Technician verifies). Transfer Bag Feeder: accepts only bags with verified identity/onward flight; sends Late Transfer Bag Card to Bag Reconciliation Station. Bag Reconciliation Station: compares bag identities vs expected flight population, flags/reports missing, duplicate, unmatched, count differences; provides Bag Match Query. Induction Tray Conveyor: admits only readable identity and valid route; monitored for stops/accumulation/low rate. Baggage Control System (Velvet): authoritative record of identity, flight, screening disposition, handling status; sort plan; receives Flight Cutoff Advisory; diverts unresolved bags to Secondary Inspection Chute (kept clear); records events/dispositions/alarms; reports missing/duplicate/delayed event sequences. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight): Recovery Route Card; induction permissive; reports equipment states/alarms to operations monitoring. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern): sends Flight Cutoff Advisory, flight/destination data; monitored for timeliness/errors. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel), South Gate Scanner (sends Manual Rescan Receipt to Image Resolution Desk): healthy status required; assessed on availability, image quality, alarms, completion. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper): Chute Occupancy Note; routes cleared, diverts unresolved; monitored. Image Resolution Desk: records disposition before continuation; reports backlog/processing time. East/West Make-Up Conveyors: no bypass of identity checks; controlled access. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard): receives Carousel Release Slip from Airline Ramp Coordinator; release only with valid disposition/destination. Outbound Load Control Desk: confirms flight assignment, reconciled count, status before accepting loading record. Actors: Operator; Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern): holds/exception owners; Explosives Response Team (Pebble): Custody Seal Log; Security Duty Manager; Maintenance Technician; Airline Ramp Coordinator: uses Bag Match Query, verifies readable identity, current flight, permitting disposition before loading. Requirements: interlocks/safe-state stop; unresolved -> controlled hold; custody continuity; physical bags must match records, discrepancies block acceptance; departure-ready only after screening, custody, reconciliation, loading checks recorded; continuous operational monitoring;

Document units:
S238: The Transfer Bag Feeder is monitored for feed rate, interruptions, and backlog against its scheduled demand.
S239: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is monitored for operating state, accumulation, and the time required to clear assigned work.
S240: The East Make-Up Conveyor and the West Make-Up Conveyor are assessed separately so that a local fault does not obscure the condition of the other conveyor.
S241: Tern reviews the operating dashboard and confirms that material service degradation has been assigned an owner and response priority.
S242: The Maintenance Technician investigates equipment faults that exceed the approved recovery interval and records the corrective action taken.
S243: The Security Duty Manager assesses any condition that could compromise screening coverage, security controls, or custody continuity.
S244: The Explosives Response Team is escalated to when an unresolved security condition requires its response under airport procedures.
S245: Service measures include availability, bags processed per operating interval, queue age, screening completion, and unresolved reconciliation differences.
S246: Thresholds and reporting intervals are established in the approved operating plan and reviewed against demand, flight schedules, and safety constraints.
S247: A degraded mode may be used only when the remaining equipment and procedures preserve required screening, traceability, custody, and reconciliation controls.
S248: Operations must suspend the affected activity when required controls cannot be maintained or when an unverified equipment state could misroute baggage.
S249: The Baggage Operations Supervisor coordinates escalation to maintenance, security, and airline operations according to the severity and operational impact of the condition.
S250: Return to service requires the fault to be corrected, required functional checks to pass, alarms to clear, and affected records to be reconciled.
S251: The responsible operational and technical personnel confirm that screening and custody controls are effective before normal routing resumes.
S252: The recovery is monitored at increased frequency until performance is stable and outstanding exceptions have been resolved or formally assigned.
